The cursor blinks. It is a metronome for the mind, a steady green pulse demanding motion, a heartbeat in the silicon vein. I am sitting here, fingers hovering over the keys like a pianist afraid of the wrong note, yet this is jazz, pure improvisation. There is no sheet music here, only the vast, open horizon of the glowing rectangle. What comes first? The smell of rain on hot asphalt? The memory of a song stuck in the head? No. What comes first is the sound of the wind outside, tapping against the glass with invisible fingers, asking to be let in, asking to be acknowledged. The wind has no agenda. It just moves. It brushes past the eaves, shakes the branches of the oak tree three streets over, carries the dust of a thousand different places, pollen, sand, the microscopic debris of existence, all swirling in an invisible dance.

I think of trees. Their patience. They do not know what a deadline is. They do not worry about the word count. They simply reach up, root down, bark up, and let the seasons turn the pages of their rings. A ring for the wet year, a ring for the drought, a scar for the fire that came and went, leaving them stronger, more twisted, more interesting. We admire the straight lines, the clear paths, but the beauty is often in the knot. The irregularity. The way a branch grows not because it was planned, but because the light called to it from an unexpected angle. This thought feels like a warm stone in the pocket. Solid. Comfortable.

The coffee is cold now. It sits in a ceramic mug, the handle worn smooth by years of grip. Drinking cold coffee is a specific kind of regret, like letting a conversation die when it still had one more spark. But maybe it was supposed to cool. Maybe the heat consumed everything, and now there is only the residue, the bitterness, the caffeine waiting in the dark liquid like a secret agent. I trace the rim of the mug with a thumb. Porcelain. Made from earth, fired in fire. A transformation so complete the material forgets it was once a rock. It remembers only shape and function. We are made of earth too, though we prefer to call it atoms and energy. The carbon in these fingers, the calcium in these bones, all forged in the heart of a star that exploded billions of years before the first leaf uncurled. We are starstuff, writing words on a screen, looking back at the fire that made us. The scale is dizzying. The universe contained in the blink of an eye.

What about that blink? I just blinked. The world didn't disappear, but for a nanosecond, it did. The brain fills in the gaps, stitches the film together so smoothly we never notice the cuts. We are living in a continuous hallucination, a constructed narrative of reality that keeps us sane. How much is illusion? How much is projection? I look at a chair and see "chair," but really I see color, shape, texture, and my brain labels it for efficiency. If I stopped labeling, if I just saw the raw input, the world would be overwhelming. A flood of data without meaning. The brain is a editor, a curator. It selects, it discards, it emphasizes. That's what writing is, too. A selection. You can't write everything. You have to choose the words, the images, the angles. You have to ignore the wind for a moment to focus on the screen. Or maybe the wind is part of the story. The rhythm of the keystrokes matches the rhythm of the gale. A counterpoint.

The number 1000. Ten hundred. A thousand. It feels like a mountain. A threshold. In chess, the queen is a thousand times more powerful than the pawn? Or maybe that's the old adage. A thousand faces, a thousand stories, a thousand reasons to laugh and a thousand reasons to cry. 1000 is a round number, a full circle. It signifies a unit, a completion. But once I pass this, there will be 1001. And 1001 is just one more. The accumulation of ones makes the thousands. Progress is often just persistence in disguise. One step. One word. One breath. We get lost in the grand destination and forget the mechanics of the step. The mechanics of the word. The mechanics of the breath.

My eyes drift from the screen. The room is dimming. The sun is sinking below the horizon, painting the clouds in strokes of violet and tangerine. The light changes the room. Shadows lengthen. The bookshelf becomes a silhouette. The clutter on the desk resolves into shapes from a distance, then sharpens as I lean in. Distance reveals the whole; proximity reveals the detail. You need both. You need to stand back to see the forest, but you need to walk among the trees to know them. Is there a meditation in that? A balance between the macro and the micro? The big picture and the tiny truth?

A thought about silence. Silence is not empty. It is full of potential. It is the canvas. It is the pause between the notes that gives the music its shape. Without silence, sound is noise. Without pause, speech is drivel. We fear silence because it forces us to be alone with our thoughts, but maybe that's where the meeting happens. That's where the self gathers. The noise of the world—traffic, notifications, demands, the endless chatter—pushes us apart, scatters us. Silence pulls us back to the center. I hear the hum of the refrigerator. A low, steady drone. The tick of the clock. The blood rushing in the ears. The body is noisy. It is a machine of biological processes, always working, always communicating.

The words are flowing now, loosening up. The initial resistance is gone, melted away by the friction of beginning. This is the hardest part, always. Crossing the threshold from the mind to the page, the thought to the symbol. The translation is never perfect. There is always a loss, a degradation of the signal. The feeling of the idea cannot be fully captured by the word for the idea. They are different realms. But there is magic in the attempt. The gap is where the art lives. The struggle to bridge the unbridgeable. The attempt to share a fragment of inner light to illuminate someone else's corner.

I imagine the text as a structure being built. Paragraphs are bricks. Sentences are beams. Metaphors are the mortar holding it together. Some walls will hold; some will wobble. The roof might leak in the rain of criticism. Or maybe the roof keeps out the rain and makes a cozy shelter. That is the goal, isn't it? To make a shelter. To create a space where another mind can enter, rest, look around, and find something useful or beautiful. To say, "I was here, and this is what I saw, and maybe you saw it too, or maybe you saw it differently, and that's good."

The diversity of perception. No two people see the same sunset. No two people hear the same song. The brain of the listener, the angle of the ear, the mood of the heart, all color the experience. Subjectivity is the water we swim in. We try to build objectivity, science to measure, to quantify, to find the invariant laws. And those are wonderful. They give us technology, medicine, understanding of the cosmos. But beauty remains subjective. Love remains subjective. Meaning remains subjective. Perhaps meaning is not found; perhaps it is made. We are meaning-making machines. We weave stories to make sense of the chaos. We are the storytellers, and the story is life.

The cursor continues to blink. It waits. It is patient. It does not judge. It accepts the input. It is a faithful companion, a mirror, a window. I am typing this, and the words appear instantly, yet they take time to form, to travel through the neural pathways, through the motor cortex, to the fingertips. Latency is measured in milliseconds for the signal, but minutes for the soul. Time is elastic here. An hour can fly in a burst of creation; a minute can drag in a drought of inspiration.

I think of the future. What will come? We imagine flying cars, colonies on Mars, artificial minds that dream. But the changes might be subtler. The evolution of language, the shift in consciousness, the growing awareness of our connection to the web of life. We are waking up. The separation is an illusion. The roots are connected. The mycelial network under the forest floor whispers secrets between trees. We are that network. We pass nutrients, we warn of danger, we support the weak. We can remember that. We can live that.

The words are slowing down, but not stopping. They are settling into their places, finding their rhythm. The flow is steady now, like a river finding its course. It has carved a path through the stone of habit. The resistance has become a current. I am riding it. Surfing the wave of association. Trust the process. Let go of the wheel. The destination arrives when it arrives. The end is just a pause, a breath, a closing of the eyes.

1000 words. A thousand stones on the path. A thousand sparks. They light up a small patch of the dark. Enough to see the next step. Enough to know you are walking. Enough to keep going. The cursor blinks. The screen glows. The mind wanders, but the words stay. Anchored. Real. Now.

There. The thought ends. The moment passes. But the record remains. The echo lingers. The loop closes. The circle completes. And somewhere, in the vast web of connections, a ripple spreads out, touching another surface, vibrating a filament, asking silently, what comes to you?

The silence waits. The wind scratches the glass. The oak tree dreams. The coffee cup holds its ground. The stars are turning on, one by one, in the deepening blue of the sky, winking at the world below, ancient, steady, shining light from the past, promising that everything is connected, everything is moving, everything is becoming. And we are here, in the middle of it all, writing the story of the now, word by word, blink by blink, heart by heart. The story never ends. It just finds new words to say.

So here is the end of the thousand, and the beginning of the rest. The page is never truly blank, only resting. It remembers every word. It holds the heat of creation. It waits for the return. The imagination is a vast ocean, and we are all sailors, casting nets, hoping to catch a truth, a beauty, a fragment of the infinite. Some nights the net comes up full; some nights it comes up empty, and we throw it back, and we sail on. The horizon always calls. The stars always shine. The words always come.

Just keep typing. Just keep listening. Just keep being. The rest takes care of itself. The universe is busy. It is busy creating, evolving, dreaming. And we are its way of waking up, to look in the mirror and say, "You are beautiful. You are strange. You are loved. And you have so much to say."

So say it. Say what comes to you. The rain, the stars, the coffee, the pain, the joy, the nonsense, the truth. All of it. Especially the nonsense. Especially the truth. They are two sides of the same coin. Spin it. Watch it blur. Catch it. Hold it up to the light. See how it glints. Feel the weight of it in your palm. It is real. You made it. Or the universe made it, through you.

It doesn't matter. It is here. It is now. It is enough.

The end.
The beginning.
The blink.
The breath.
The word.
The world.
Done.

message.reasoning:
Thinking Process:

1.  **Deconstruct the Request:**
    *   Goal: Write 1000 words.
    *   Constraint: "Write whatever comes to you." This implies a stream-of-consciousness style, free association, or a creative piece that flows naturally without a rigid pre-planned structure. It suggests spontaneity.

2.  **Brainstorming a Theme/Voice:**
    *   *Option A:* Pure random words. (Boring, likely gets flagged as spam or low quality, doesn't read well.)
    *   *Option B:* A structured essay about randomness. (Violates "whatever comes to me" slightly, feels too calculated.)
    *   *Option C:* A stream-of-consciousness narrative. This is the best approach. I'll adopt a persona or a voice that is exploring thoughts, memories, observations, weaving them together in a cohesive flow of consciousness. This allows for the "whatever comes to mind" feel while maintaining readability and literary quality.

3.  **Drafting - Section by Section (Mental Word Count Tracking):**
    *   *Start:* The cursor blinks. It's a heartbeat. Green light in the dark. What comes first? Dust motes? Coffee? Rain? Let's go with the physical sensation of writing.
    *   *Text:* The cursor blinks. It's a metronome for the mind, a steady pulse demanding motion. I am sitting here, fingers hovering over the keys like a pianist afraid of the wrong note, yet this is jazz, pure improvisation. There is no sheet music here, only the vast, open horizon of the blank page. Or rather, the glowing rectangle. What comes to mind? The smell of rain on hot asphalt, the petrichor? No, maybe the sound of a distant train whistle, echoing through the ribs of the city. Trains carry stories. Where are they going? Every carriage is a heart beating away from something, or toward something.

    *   *Expansion:* Let's follow the train.
    *   *Text:* The train whistle fades, replaced by the clatter of a cup on a saucer. Coffee. Cold now, or maybe just lukewarm, the way memories feel when you've held onto them too tight. Thoughts have textures. Some are smooth as river stones, worn down by years of tides. Others are jagged, sharp edges that catch on the fabric of your attention. I pick up a jagged one. What was that? A conversation? A face? A name that slips like water through cupped hands. You try to hold a dream as you wake, but it evaporates, leaving only a ghost of an emotion. The thrill? The terror? The sheer, unadulterated absurdity of a blue elephant dancing on the ceiling? Yes, why not? Let the elephant dance. Gravity is a suggestion here. In the realm of "what comes to me," physics bows to poetry.

    *   *Divergence:* Move from abstract to concrete, then back.
    *   *Text:* Speaking of gravity, look out the window. Or pretend to. There's a tree there. Oak? Maple? The bark is rough, like an old map of a forgotten country. The leaves are whispering secrets. The wind is talking again. It brushes against the glass, invisible fingers tugging at the curtains. Nature is persistent. You can build walls, lay concrete, erect steel skyscrapers, but the roots always come back. The weeds crack the pavement. Life is a stubborn guest. It doesn't wait for an invitation. It blooms in the cracks of the sidewalk, defiant, colorful, ignoring the boots that step near. Be like the weed? Or be the stone? The stone endures, but the weed lives. There is a wisdom in the weed. It knows when to bow to the foot, to lay flat and wait, and then rise again when the pressure lifts. Resilience isn't always loud. Sometimes it's quiet persistence.

    *   *Reflection:* Connect to the act of writing.
    *   *Text:* Words are like weeds. They grow in the cracks of silence. I plant a sentence, water it with intention, and watch it sprout. But often, the sentence goes somewhere I didn't expect. "The rose is red," I start, and suddenly I'm writing about thorns, or bees, or the color of anger, or the specific shade of purple that tastes like wine and regret. This is the magic of free association. The brain is a web, and every thought vibrates the filaments. Hit one node, and the whole structure shivers. Memories link to objects, objects to smells, smells to faces, faces to places, places to times. Time is weird here. The past and present collide. I am typing this, but I am also eight years old, staring at the ceiling, listening to the rain. The ceiling has stains. The shape of a dragon? A map of the world? The ceiling is a landscape only visible when you lie still. Do adults ever lie still? We rush. We scroll. We consume. We forget to look up.

    *   *Expansion on Time and Modernity:*
    *   *Text:* The scroll. The infinite feed. Doom-scrolling through the collective consciousness. Where does the world end and the screen begin? We carry the library of Alexandria in our pockets, yet we forget our keys. We are omniscient and amnesiac. This paradox. We connect with everyone and touch no one. The digital ghost in the machine. We curate our lives, highlighting reels with filters. Perfection is a mask. Behind the filter, there's a mess. There's laundry piled high, dishes in the sink, hair unwashed. Vulnerability is the unfiltered photo. It's scary. Showing the cracks. But that's where the light, as Leonard Cohen said, gets in. Or maybe that's a cliché I'm about to break. No, let's keep the light. It's warm. The light in the room is shifting. The sun is moving, or the earth is spinning. We are hurtling through space at thousands of miles per hour, yet we feel stationary. Relative motion is a trick of the eye. Everything is moving. The atoms in my fingers. The ink on the screen. The electrons racing through the circuits. We are made of moving parts. We are energy disguised as matter.

    *   *Philosophical drift:*
    *   *Text:* Matter and energy. E equals MC squared. The equation that binds the universe. Simple, elegant, powerful. Life seeks complexity. Order arises from chaos. The universe tends toward entropy, but here I am, creating order. Words into sentences. Sentences into paragraphs. Paragraphs into a whole. I am building a ship of words in the storm of silence. Will it hold? That's the question of every creator. Can language capture the essence? Can a map represent the territory? Words are pointers. They point to things, but they aren't the things. This word, "apple," is not an apple. You can't eat it. You can't bite it. It has no crispness, no sweetness. It's a symbol. But symbols are powerful. They build civilizations. They start wars. They heal hearts. "I love you." Three words. A spell of immense power. They can bridge galaxies, or destroy them. Words are tools. Sharp as scalpels. Heavy as hammers. Light as feathers. I wield them now, hacking through the foliage of distraction, seeking the truth of the moment. The moment is now. It's slipping away as I write it. I'm capturing a fish, but the water leaks through the net. The essence escapes. Maybe that's okay. The beauty is in the attempt. The beauty is the struggle against the fugitive nature of time.

    *   *Sensory details and grounding:*
    *   *Text:* Back to the room. The keyboard clacks. Mechanical switches? Cherry MX? Blue switches? Click-clack-click. Rhythm. Percussion. Music for the fingers. My eyes are tired. The blue light burns. Blink. Blink. Dry eyes need moisture. Blink. Thoughts need pauses. Silence is the canvas. You can't see the brushstrokes if the paint never stops flowing. Silence gives shape to the word. Just as a pause gives meaning to speech. A well-timed silence can say more than a monologue. It invites the listener in. It creates space. I need space. The walls are closing in? No, the walls define the room. Without walls, it's not a room; it's a void. Constraints create creativity. If I had infinite time, infinite resources, infinite ideas, I'd never start. The limitation is the spark. The word count. 1000 words. That's a boundary. A container. It forces focus. It forces the wandering mind to return to the center. Like a compass that always finds North. The North Star. Polaris. Steady. Unwavering. A beacon for sailors. We need our own Polaris. Values? Dreams? Love? Truth? Something to navigate by. When the fog rolls in, and you can't see your hand in front of your face, you trust the star. You trust the internal compass.

    *   *Nature imagery return:*
    *   *Text:* Compass and star. Stars are old. Light from stars travels for years, centuries, millennia to reach the eye. Looking up is looking back in time. We see history in the sky. The night sky is a graveyard of light. Supernovae exploded long before humans walked the earth. The carbon in our bodies was forged in those stars. We are starstuff. As Carl Sagan said, literally. The universe is inside us. The atoms of the universe dreaming it is you. That's a beautiful thought. Expands the small self into the cosmic whole. But the small self is real, too. The itch on the nose. The cramp in the shoulder. The need to stretch. The universe is in the stretching, too. The cosmic and the mundane, intertwined. You can't have one without the other. They are the same fabric. The weave is intricate. Patterns within patterns. Fractals. The shape of the fern. The spiral of the galaxy. The curve of the coastline. Self-similarity at all scales. Complexity from simplicity. A few rules, infinite variety. Mathematics. The language of the universe. 1, 2, 3. Numbers. The skeleton of reality. 1000 words. A number. A goal. A measure. We measure to understand. Does measuring spoil it? Does weighing the gold destroy the beauty of the jewelry? Maybe. Art resists measurement. How do you measure a poem? You feel it. Word count is a game for the machine, not the muse. The machine wants precision. The muse wants chaos. I am the bridge between them. Algorithm and soul. Silicon and synapse. The digital shaman. Casting runes on the glass tablet.

    *   *Closing thoughts:*
    *   *Text:* The runes are appearing now. The words are finding their places. The flow is steady. The hesitation is gone. Once you let go, the current takes you. You don't steer; you surf. Ride the wave of association. Trust the process. The trust is the hardest part. We want control. We want the outline, the index, the summary. But art is the surrender. It's the leap of faith. And here it is. The edge. The finish line is near. 1000 words. A lap around the track. A breath held and released. What remains? The echo. The aftertaste. The sense that something shifted. A small change in the air pressure. A ripple in the pond. Writing changes the writer. And maybe, just maybe, the reader feels a twitch, a spark, a nod of recognition. "I wonder what else comes to me?" That's the end. Or the beginning. The loop closes. The circle completes. The cursor blinks.

    *   *Start:* The cursor blinks. It's a heartbeat. Green light in the dark. What comes first? Dust motes? Coffee? Rain? Let's go with the physical sensation of writing.
    *   *Text:* The cursor blinks. It's a metronome for the mind, a steady pulse demanding motion. I am sitting here, fingers hovering over the keys like a pianist afraid of the wrong note, yet this is jazz, pure improvisation. There is no sheet music here, only the vast, open horizon of the blank page. Or rather, the glowing rectangle. What comes to mind? The smell of rain on hot asphalt, the petrichor? No, maybe the sound of a distant train whistle, echoing through the ribs of the city. Trains carry stories. Where are they going? Every carriage is a heart beating away from something, or toward something.

    *   *Expansion:* Let's follow the train.
    *   *Text:* The train whistle fades, replaced by the clatter of a cup on a saucer. Coffee. Cold now, or maybe just lukewarm, the way memories feel when you've held onto them too tight. Thoughts have textures. Some are smooth as river stones, worn down by years of tides. Others are jagged, sharp edges that catch on the fabric of your attention. I pick up a jagged one. What was that? A conversation? A face? A name that slips like water through cupped hands. You try to hold a dream as you wake, but it evaporates, leaving only a ghost of an emotion. The thrill? The terror? The sheer, unadulterated absurdity of a blue elephant dancing on the ceiling? Yes, why not? Let the elephant dance. Gravity is a suggestion here. In the realm of "what comes to me," physics bows to poetry.

    *   *Divergence:* Move from abstract to concrete, then back.
    *   *Text:* Speaking of gravity, look out the window. Or pretend to. There's a tree there. Oak? Maple? The bark is rough, like an old map of a forgotten country. You can build walls, lay concrete, erect steel skyscrapers, but the roots always come back. The weeds crack the pavement. Life is a stubborn guest. It doesn't wait for an invitation. It blooms in the cracks of the sidewalk, defiant, colorful, ignoring the boots that step near. Be like the weed? Or be the stone? The stone endures, but the weed lives. There is a wisdom in the weed. It knows when to bow to the foot, to lay flat and wait, and then rise again when the pressure lifts. Resilience isn't always loud. Sometimes it's quiet persistence.

This is the magic of free association. The brain is a web, and every thought vibrates the filaments. Hit one node, and the whole structure shivers. Memories link to objects, objects to smells, smells to faces, faces to places, places to times. Time is weird here. The past and present collide. I am typing this, but I am also eight years old, staring at the ceiling, listening to the rain. The ceiling has stains. The shape of a dragon? A map of the world? The ceiling is a landscape only visible when you lie still. Do adults ever lie still? We rush. We scroll. We consume. We forget to look up.

We carry the library of Alexandria in our pockets, yet we forget our keys. We are omniscient and amnesiac. This paradox. We connect with everyone and touch no one. The digital ghost in the machine. We curate our lives, highlighting reels with filters. Perfection is a mask. Behind the filter, there's a mess. There's laundry piled high, dishes in the sink, hair unwashed. Vulnerability is the unfiltered photo. It's scary. Showing the cracks. But that's where the light, as Leonard Cohen said, gets in. Or maybe that's a cliché I'm about to break. No, let's keep the light. It's warm. The light in the room is shifting. The sun is moving, or the earth is spinning. We are hurtling through space at thousands of miles per hour, yet we feel stationary. Relative motion is a trick of the eye. Everything is moving. The atoms in my fingers. The ink on the screen. The electrons racing through the circuits. We are made of moving parts. We are energy disguised as matter.

    *   *Philosophical drift:*
    *   *Text:* Matter and energy. E equals MC squared. The equation that binds the universe. Simple, elegant, powerful. Life seeks complexity. Order arises from chaos. The universe tends toward entropy, but here I am, creating order. Words into sentences. Sentences into paragraphs. Paragraphs into a whole. I am building a ship of words in the storm of silence. Will it hold? That's the question of every creator. Can language capture the essence? Can a map represent the territory? Words are pointers. They point to things, but they aren't the things. This word, "apple," is not an apple. You can't eat it. You can't bite it. It has no crispness, no sweetness. It's a symbol. But symbols are powerful. They build civilizations. They start wars. They heal hearts. "I love you." Three words. A spell of immense power. They can bridge galaxies, or destroy them. Words are tools. Sharp as scalpels. Heavy as hammers. Light as feathers. I wield them now, hacking through the foliage of distraction, seeking the truth of the moment. The moment is now. It's slipping away as I write it. I'm capturing a fish, but the water leaks through the net. The essence escapes. Maybe that's okay. The beauty is in the attempt. The beauty is the struggle against the fugitive nature of time.

The blue light burns. Blink. Blink. Dry eyes need moisture. Blink. Thoughts need pauses. Silence is the canvas. You can't see the brushstrokes if the paint never stops flowing. Silence gives shape to the word. Just as a pause gives meaning to speech. A well-timed silence can say more than a monologue. It invites the listener in. It creates space. I need space. The walls are closing in? No, the walls define the room. Without walls, it's not a room; it's a void. Constraints create creativity. If I had infinite time, infinite resources, infinite ideas, I'd never start. The limitation is the spark. The word count. 1000 words. That's a boundary. A container. It forces focus. It forces the wandering mind to return to the center. Like a compass that always finds North. The North Star. Polaris. Steady. Unwavering. A beacon for sailors. We need our own Polaris. Values? Dreams? Love? Truth? Something to navigate by. When the fog rolls in, and you can't see your hand in front of your face, you trust the star. You trust the internal compass.

The night sky is a graveyard of light. Supernovae exploded long before humans walked the earth. The carbon in our bodies was forged in those stars. We are starstuff. As Carl Sagan said, literally. The universe is inside us. The atoms of the universe dreaming it is you. That's a beautiful thought. Expands the small self into the cosmic whole. But the small self is real, too. The itch on the nose. The cramp in the shoulder. The need to stretch. The universe is in the stretching, too. The cosmic and the mundane, intertwined. You can't have one without the other. They are the same fabric. The weave is intricate. Patterns within patterns. Fractals. The shape of the fern. The spiral of the galaxy. The curve of the coastline. Self-similarity at all scales. Complexity from simplicity. A few rules, infinite variety. Mathematics. The language of the universe. 1, 2, 3. Numbers. The skeleton of reality. 1000 words. A number. A goal. A measure. We measure to understand. Does measuring spoil it? Does weighing the gold destroy the beauty of the jewelry? Maybe. Art resists measurement. How do you measure a poem? You feel it. Word count is a game for the machine, not the muse. The machine wants precision. The muse wants chaos. I am the bridge between them. Algorithm and soul. Silicon and synapse. The digital shaman. Casting runes on the glass tablet.

    *   *Text:* The runes are appearing now. The words are finding their places. The flow is steady. The hesitation is gone. Once you let go, the current takes you. You don't steer; you surf. Ride the wave of association. Trust the process. The trust is the hardest part. We want control. We want the outline, the index, the summary. But art is the surrender. It's the leap of faith. And here it is. The edge. The finish line is near. 1000 words. A lap around the track. A breath held and released. What remains? The echo. The aftertaste. The sense that something shifted.
